reviews.review:
For context, I have never played the original RoR but 100%ed RoR2

I do not like this game.

First, some stuff it does quite well. Like you're used to from the Risk of Rain series, there's a lot of characters, all with unlockable skills as well as tons of items to unlock. There's quite a variation in level visuals and there's lots of enemies to fight.
You also start with 4 skins for each character, I assume this is to make it easier to see who's who in a multiplayer session, although the skins can also be used in singleplayer.

There are also challenges you can do to unlock new items or abilities for characters. While I absolutely hate some of them for how insanely difficult and annoying they can be, I like the idea.

Now onto the stuff I don't like.
First, let's start with the survivors. While they look nice for being in 2D now, I am a bit confused as to why they didn't just use the same starting loadouts as in RoR2. While I understand that some changes are just required to make the game more interesting and some skills need to be changed to fit the new 2D format, I see these characters I am familiar with but then they have just different skills or playstyles than they had when you unlocked them in RoR2. Some don't even have new skills and they just swapped around which skill has to be unlocked and which one you get by default.

I feel like the next part should be the controls. I used a controller, like I do with any 2D / topdown game. It feels bad to play. The movement is fun (when they don't force you to do parkour with small platforms and you got like insane speed due to some items) but the shooting is awful. You, as the player, can only shoot either left or right, which would be fine if there weren't a lot of enemies that just fly all around you or above you or have some attacks that cause them to be in the air. I don't get why they didn't add auto and manual aim in more than 2 directions, since this makes everything so much more frustrating than it has to be.
Climbing ropes also seems to just not work half the time. I thought the issue might be that I was trying to attack and grab onto one and not attacking seemed to help sometimes, but not consistently.

The levels at first seem quite nice, they have decent visuals although get repetitive quite quickly, but overall, fine, visually at least. In terms of gamedesign they are just awful. The maps that I have played are all just platforms with ropes, that's pretty much what it boils down to. Sure there are jump pads too that you cannot jump over so if you wanna get to whatever is on the other side of one, you might be forced to take damage, but aside from that, there are only 2 levels that I have seen that feel unique. There is the underwater level, which has underwater physics (just lower gravity and no fall damage which is nice) and the (final) train level which has these keycards you can use to open up doors. The rest are all visually different and different enemies will spawn, but it's not like each map has a unique gimmick that makes them stand out on anything (at least not from what I noticed).
Now you think that that might've been it on level design, but no, it's not.
There's these little areas in every map that holds a little secret. Sometimes an item, sometimes some shards or legendary chests. There is no obvious way in so what is the solution? Hug every wall, try going down on every path, just to see if you can walk through a wall or climb down an invisible rope. Games need to have some sort of indicator as to when there is a secret that needs to be found. The fact that the train level had an invisible rope in the middle of a crate with no indication that it was there, is stupid. This will just make people wonder where the secrets are all the time, and not in a way that causes players to actually think, but in a way that causes them to try and walk/jump through every wall and hug every surface they can find. It's awful gamedesign.

The enemies for the most part are fine. Flying enemies, like I said, are the worst and some enemies hit really hard, which would be fine in a 3D environment because there is cover to hide behind and more places to go, but in 2D, it is just really hard to dodge, if your character has an ability like that at all.
The bosses are okay, they look great but can be really really hard in a 2D environment like this. The 2D part is not what makes them unfun, but the level design is. Fighting a boss in a tiny area when they are like 20 times your size, combined with all the other monsters that spawn, isn't fair.
The boss in the train level is even more stupid and unfair. Constant lasers, constantly flying in the air, teleporting all over the place. The good thing about this fight is that the area you fight them in is at least big enough to run around in.

Lastly I want to mention the visual effects. While it looks great, combine that with all the monsters running around plus maybe a couple elite bosses (shrines of the mountain), it becomes nearly impossible to see what is going on.

Overall, it's a shame. I was really excited to see what a 2D take on RoR2 could look like, I'm afraid this isn't quite it. Perhaps I was expecting too much but that doesn't change that this game is just unfair and to be honest not that fun. Not the worst game ever, but I certainly didn't enjoy most of my time spent in this game.
Great game, tons of fun. Me and my brother play this game and we have a blast!
Don't support people turning games into Spyware. Gearbox is terrible.

I love the Risk of Rain series, but it feels like Hopoo Games has moved on. After Gearbox acquired ROR2, the quality noticeably declined (e.g., Seekers of the Storm).

I bought RORR hoping for the same passion as the original, but it seems to lack that level of care. I’d still recommend it to newcomers, but don’t expect major advancements—just a bit of polish.
